newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Khulani buys stake in Springbok Patrols.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Khulani buys stake in Springbok Patrols.

text.p: South Africa's largest privately-owned security firm Springbok Patrols Ltd said on Friday black-owned Khulani Holdings Ltd had bought a 51 percent stake in it in a deal worth nearly 50 million rand.
The Bartmann family will retain 49 percent and keep management control. The deal, which will see the firm's name changed to Khulani Springbok Patrols, is effective March 1.

"We have decided to sell the majority stake in Springbok Patrols to a business that moves in the disenfranchised sector," said Mick Bartmann, head of Springbok Patrols and now deputy chairman of the new company.
Khulani is seen bringing in new clients for the firm.
Senzele Mhlungu, Khulani's chief executive and chairman of Khulani Springbok Patrols said Khulani would push for black empowerment within the new company.
Springbok employs some 12,000 security officers in South Africa and Namibia.
